report:
## Conclusion

You are correct: the evidence overwhelmingly indicates that **arthroscopy does not help with knee osteoarthritis** for the vast majority of patients.

### Key Evidence

1. **Landmark RCT (2002):** A randomized, placebo-controlled trial published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* found that arthroscopic surgery was no more effective than sham (placebo) surgery in relieving pain or improving function in patients with knee osteoarthritis. ([https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa013259](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa013259))

2. **Cochrane Review (2022):** A Cochrane review assessed arthroscopic surgery (debridement, partial meniscectomy, or both) versus placebo surgery or non-surgical treatment for degenerative knee disease, reinforcing the lack of benefit. ([https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD014328_arthroscopic-surgery-degenerative-knee-disease](https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD014328_arthroscopic-surgery-degenerative-knee-disease))

3. **Guideline Recommendations:** Multiple RCTs and the Cochrane review led NICE (UK) to recommend that arthroscopy **not** be used in the vast majority of knee osteoarthritis patients. A clinical practice guideline panel similarly recommended against arthroscopic knee surgery for degenerative knee disease. ([https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4435528/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4435528/)) ([https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323203463_Arthroscopic_surgery_for_degenerative_knee_arthritis_and_meniscal_tears_a_clinical_practice_guideline](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323203463_Arthroscopic_surgery_for_degenerative_knee_arthritis_and_meniscal_tears_a_clinical_practice_guideline))

4. **Recent Meta-analysis (2024):** A systematic review and meta-analysis concluded that arthroscopic surgery is **not superior to conservative treatment** for knee osteoarthritis. ([https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12891-024-07813-3](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12891-024-07813-3))

### Nuance

Some surgeons argue arthroscopy may benefit a **select group**—those with mild osteoarthritis and an associated meniscal tear—but higher-quality evidence is still needed to define this role. ([https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4318803/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4318803/))
